audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is the recovered polynomial degree validated before truncation in recover_polynomialcoeff?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The property asks whether recover_polynomialcoeff validates polynomial degree before truncation to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. The Go code in ReconstructDataColumnSidecars calls kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs which calls ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. No polynomial coefficient array is exposed in Go - the function returns CellsAndProofs (cells+proofs bytes). The recover_polynomialcoeff function is entirely internal to the c-kzg-4844 C library. The Go wrapper has no visibility into intermediate polynomial degree state.
phase1.state_space_analysis: State space of Go code: (cellIndices []uint64, partialCells []Cell) -> (CellsAndProofs, error). The polynomial recovery internals (degree checking, truncation) exist exclusively within the C library's opaque implementation. There is no intermediate state accessible to Go code where polynomial degree could be inspected or validated.
potential_violations: If c-kzg-4844 had a bug in degree validation, it would be a C library bug, not a Prysm Go bug
No Go-level degree validation is possible since polynomial coefficients are never materialized in Go

phase2.symbolic_execution: RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs(cellIndices, partialCells) -> type conversion -> ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs(cellIndices, ckzgPartialCells) -> (ckzgCells, ckzgProofs, err). If err != nil, error is returned. No polynomial degree validation occurs in Go because no polynomial representation exists in Go.
attack_scenarios: An attacker cannot trigger a Go-level degree violation because no such check exists in Go
Even if c-kzg-4844 returned malformed cells due to a degree bug, subsequent KZG proof verification would catch it
phase2.counterexample: No counterexample in Go code. The function recover_polynomialcoeff does not exist in Prysm Go codebase.

phase2_5.adversarial_analysis: An adversary auditing Prysm Go code cannot find a polynomial degree validation gap because there is no such check - the entire operation is delegated to c-kzg-4844. The adversary attack surface in Go is limited to inputs passed to the C library and output handling (error propagation), both correctly implemented.
phase2_5.exploitation_feasibility: Not exploitable at Go level. Any exploitation would require a bug in c-kzg-4844.

phase3.invariant_proving: Invariant: 'All polynomial degree validation is the responsibility of c-kzg-4844'. Holds by construction - the Go code has no polynomial representation. Go wrapper correctly forwards errors from the C library.
phase3.mathematical_guarantee: The Go code provides no polynomial-level guarantees because it operates on opaque cell/proof byte arrays. Mathematical guarantees are entirely provided by c-kzg-4844's EIP-7594 implementation.

phase3_5.final_verdict: Out of scope for Go audit. recover_polynomialcoeff and its polynomial degree validation are implemented exclusively in the c-kzg-4844 C library. No Go-level vulnerability exists.
phase3_5.reasoning: The Go code in Prysm does not implement recover_polynomialcoeff. kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs is a thin wrapper that type-converts inputs, calls ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs, and propagates errors. This item should be directed to the c-kzg-4844 audit scope.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the validator node detect and reject incorrect polynomials from recovery?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The property asks whether a validator can detect incorrect polynomials from recovery. Abstract states: (1) gossip validation of incoming sidecars - KZG proofs verified via VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs before storage as VerifiedRODataColumn; (2) reconstruction - ReconstructDataColumnSidecars takes verified inputs, calls c-kzg-4844, marks outputs as VerifiedRODataColumn WITHOUT re-verifying KZG proofs; (3) reconstructed sidecars are saved and broadcast. Critical gap: reconstructed sidecars bypass KZG proof verification.
phase1.state_space_analysis: State machine: incoming_sidecar -> gossip_validate (KZG verified) -> reconstruction_triggered -> recover_cells_and_proofs (c-kzg-4844) -> mark_as_VerifiedRODataColumn_without_reverification -> saved_to_store -> broadcast_to_peers. The reconstruction output path completely skips VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. If c-kzg-4844 returned incorrect cells+proofs (library bug, regression, or supply chain compromise), those would propagate as 'verified' to local store and peers.
potential_violations: Reconstructed sidecars are marked VerifiedRODataColumn without KZG proof re-verification - unconditionally trusts c-kzg-4844 output
The comment 'reconstructed sidecars are also verified' is an informal assertion, not an enforced cryptographic invariant
VerifiedRODataColumn type semantic contract is violated for the reconstruction path

phase2.symbolic_execution: Trace: verified inputs (KZG proofs cryptographically checked via gossip) -> ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs returns (cells, proofs). In reconstruction.go: for _, sidecar := range reconstructedSidecars { roSidecar, _ := blocks.NewRODataColumnWithRoot(sidecar, blockRoot); verifiedRoSidecar := blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn(roSidecar) /* NO KZG verification! */; reconstructedVerifiedRoSidecars = append(..., verifiedRoSidecar) }. No call to VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs anywhere in the reconstruction path.
attack_scenarios: Scenario 1: c-kzg-4844 library compromise or supply chain attack - reconstructed sidecars with wrong data propagate as 'verified' to local store and broadcast to peers without detection at this node
Scenario 2: Future c-kzg-4844 regression in RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs - Prysm would not catch it since it does not re-verify reconstruction output
Scenario 3: Receiving peers validate via gossip pipeline, limiting network-wide propagation - but local node data store corrupted and incorrect sidecars broadcast

phase2_5.adversarial_analysis: The vulnerability requires trusting c-kzg-4844 to produce correct outputs without secondary validation. The Go comment explicitly acknowledges this trust assumption. Defense-in-depth would require re-verifying reconstructed proofs via VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. The missing verification is a real gap: the VerifiedRODataColumn semantic contract (KZG proofs cryptographically verified) is violated for reconstructed sidecars. Practical exploitation requires: (a) a bug in c-kzg-4844's RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs producing cells/proofs inconsistent with commitments, or (b) supply chain attack on the C library.
phase2_5.exploitation_feasibility: Low in practice (requires library-level issue), but represents a meaningful defense-in-depth gap. Local node data integrity depends entirely on c-kzg-4844 correctness without secondary validation.

phase3.invariant_proving: Required invariant: 'All VerifiedRODataColumn objects have had their KZG proofs cryptographically verified'. This invariant is BROKEN for reconstructed sidecars. blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn(roSidecar) is used for both: (a) gossip-validated sidecars (KZG verified), and (b) reconstructed sidecars (KZG NOT re-verified). The Go type system cannot distinguish these cases.
phase3.mathematical_guarantee: No mathematical guarantee exists at Go level that reconstructed sidecars have valid KZG proofs. The guarantee is an informal assertion about c-kzg-4844 correctness. Defense-in-depth would require calling VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs on reconstructed sidecars before marking as VerifiedRODataColumn.

phase3_5.final_verdict: Vulnerability - missing KZG proof re-verification of reconstructed sidecars. The VerifiedRODataColumn type invariant is violated: reconstructed sidecars are marked verified without cryptographic verification. While practical exploitation requires c-kzg-4844 to produce incorrect outputs, the defense-in-depth gap is real.
phase3_5.reasoning: In ReconstructDataColumnSidecars, the code marks reconstructed sidecars as VerifiedRODataColumn without calling VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. The reasoning in the comment ('inputs were verified, therefore outputs are verified') is a trust assumption not enforced by code. Fix: add VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call on reconstructedSidecars (as []RODataColumn) before wrapping with NewVerifiedRODataColumn.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Can a P2P peer craft cell data to force polynomial degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The property asks whether a P2P peer can craft cell data with polynomial degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. Abstract state: attacker-controlled sidecar enters gossip validation pipeline. The pipeline runs: ValidFields -> VerifyDataColumnSidecar (structural checks) -> SidecarInclusionProven (commitment must match signed block's blob_kzg_commitments) -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (KZG batch proof verification). KZG proofs cryptographically commit to polynomial content - forging proofs for wrong-degree polynomials requires breaking BLS12-381 discrete log.
phase1.state_space_analysis: Attacker cell state space: (cell_bytes, kzg_proof, commitment). For cell to pass KZG verification, cell_bytes must be consistent with the polynomial committed in commitment. The commitment must match the block's blob_kzg_commitments (via SidecarInclusionProven). An honest commitment encodes a polynomial of degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. The attacker cannot forge cells claiming higher degree without breaking the KZG binding assumption.
potential_violations: If KZG proof verification were skipped, attacker-crafted cells could reach reconstruction
Gossip validation pipeline mandates KZG proof verification before any sidecar is accepted

phase2.symbolic_execution: Attacker sends DataColumnSidecar with crafted cell data. Gossip validation: (1) verifier.ValidFields() structural checks; (2) verifier.SidecarInclusionProven() - KZG commitments must be in signed block - attacker cannot change; (3) validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. KZG proof verification fails for wrong polynomial content. Sidecar rejected, never stored, never used in reconstruction.
attack_scenarios: Attacker cannot provide cells with wrong polynomial degree: valid KZG proofs are computationally infeasible to forge for wrong polynomial evaluations
KZG commitment system binds cells to the committed polynomial degree
phase2.counterexample: No counterexample. The KZG proof system and gossip validation pipeline prevent this attack.

phase2_5.adversarial_analysis: A maximally adversarial peer can craft arbitrary byte sequences for cell data. However, gossip validation pipeline provides cryptographic barriers: (1) commitment must match signed block's blob_kzg_commitments (Merkle proof), (2) KZG proof must verify against commitment and cell data. Breaking these requires solving discrete log in BLS12-381.
phase2_5.exploitation_feasibility: Computationally infeasible - requires breaking BLS12-381 discrete log.

phase3.invariant_proving: Invariant: 'Cells used in reconstruction have been KZG-verified against correct commitments from a signed block'. This invariant holds: gossip validation enforces (a) commitment consistency with signed block via inclusion proof, (b) KZG proof verification for each cell. Only VerifiedRODataColumn objects (passed all gossip checks) are accepted as input to ReconstructDataColumnSidecars.
phase3.mathematical_guarantee: KZG commitment scheme provides binding commitment to polynomial. Opening proofs for evaluations must match the committed polynomial. Gossip validation cryptographically enforces this binding.

phase3_5.final_verdict: Not a vulnerability. Gossip validation pipeline's mandatory KZG proof verification and commitment inclusion proof check prevent P2P peers from injecting cells with incorrect polynomial degree into reconstruction.
phase3_5.reasoning: The attack requires bypassing cryptographic KZG proof verification (computationally infeasible). The validation pipeline correctly enforces these checks before any sidecar reaches reconstruction. No Go-level weakness enables this attack.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Is cell_index validated to be in [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) before array access in coset_shift_for_cell?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The property asks whether cell_index (column index) is validated within [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB) before coset_shift_for_cell. Go validation: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns -> ErrIndexTooLarge. Called in gossip validation via verifier.ValidFields(). Any sidecar reaching reconstruction has Index < numberOfColumns. In EIP-7594, numberOfColumns == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB == 128. Therefore Go ensures all cell indices are in [0, 128) matching c-kzg-4844's expectation.
phase1.state_space_analysis: State: sidecar.Index in [0, numberOfColumns) by gossip validation enforcement. In reconstruction: cellsIndices from sidecarByIndex map keys = sidecar.Index values, all < numberOfColumns. Per EIP-7594 config: numberOfColumns = BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns = 128 = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. Cell indices passed to c-kzg-4844 are in [0, 128), matching expected range for coset_shift_for_cell's internal array access.
potential_violations: If BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns misconfigured to > CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, indices could be outside c-kzg-4844's range - c-kzg-4844 would return error for invalid indices
Configuration mismatch is a deployment concern, not a code vulnerability

phase2.symbolic_execution: Trace: sidecar.Index = X. Gossip validation: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks X >= numberOfColumns (128), returns ErrIndexTooLarge if so. If X < 128, stored as VerifiedRODataColumn. In reconstruction: X added to cellsIndices. Passed to ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs. Inside c-kzg-4844, coset_shift_for_cell accesses roots_brp[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * X]. For X < 128 and FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * 128 <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB, access is within bounds.
attack_scenarios: Attacker sends sidecar with Index = 128: VerifyDataColumnSidecar returns ErrIndexTooLarge, rejected
Attacker sends sidecar with Index = UINT64_MAX: VerifyDataColumnSidecar returns ErrIndexTooLarge (UINT64_MAX >= 128)
All out-of-bounds cell indices caught at gossip validation boundary

phase2_5.adversarial_analysis: Go bounds check in VerifyDataColumnSidecar (sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns) is robust. Runs at gossip validation boundary BEFORE any sidecar is accepted. An adversary cannot bypass this check to inject out-of-bounds indices into reconstruction.
phase2_5.exploitation_feasibility: No exploitation path for correctly configured nodes. Bounds check is at P2P boundary.

phase3.invariant_proving: Invariant: 'All cell_indices passed to ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs are < numberOfColumns (= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB)'. Proof: (1) VerifyDataColumnSidecar enforces sidecar.Index < numberOfColumns. (2) VerifiedRODataColumn objects have Index < numberOfColumns. (3) ReconstructDataColumnSidecars only accepts VerifiedRODataColumn inputs. (4) cellsIndices come from map keys = sidecar.Index values. Invariant holds by chain: gossip_validation -> VerifiedRODataColumn -> reconstruction.
phase3.mathematical_guarantee: Go bounds check ensures all passed indices are in [0, numberOfColumns). With numberOfColumns = 128 = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB per EIP-7594, all indices within c-kzg-4844's expected range.

phase3_5.final_verdict: Not a vulnerability. Go gossip validation checks sidecar.Index < numberOfColumns (128 per EIP-7594) before any sidecar is accepted. This ensures all cell indices passed to c-kzg-4844 (including for coset_shift_for_cell's internal array access) are within valid range [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB).
phase3_5.reasoning: VerifyDataColumnSidecar's index bounds check (sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns -> ErrIndexTooLarge) is applied at the P2P gossip boundary. All VerifiedRODataColumn objects have been validated to have Index < numberOfColumns = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The protection is in place and correct.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002: Does cell_to_coset_evals produce exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements and validate byte segment sizes?

phase1.abstract_interpretation: The property examines whether cell_to_coset_evals output size is validated. In Prysm, Cell is defined as type Cell [BytesPerCell]byte - a fixed-size array at compile time. BytesPerCell = FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT is a compile-time constant. Structural validation: VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks len(sidecar.Column) == len(sidecar.KzgCommitments) == len(sidecar.KzgProofs). Content validation: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs via VerifyCellKZGProofBatch validates cell bytes are valid polynomial evaluations.
phase1.state_space_analysis: Cell size state: fixed at compile time. type Cell [BytesPerCell]byte. BytesPerCell is a constant (ckzg4844.BytesPerCell = 2048 bytes = 128 field elements * 32 bytes/element). A Cell value in Go always has exactly BytesPerCell bytes - Go's type system enforces this unconditionally. The ckzg4844.Cell type is also a fixed-size array matching BytesPerCell.
potential_violations: If a Cell value somehow had wrong size: impossible by Go type system
If c-kzg-4844's cell_to_coset_evals produced wrong number of elements: internal to C library, not exposed in Go

phase2.symbolic_execution: Trace: Go Cell = [BytesPerCell]byte. Converted to ckzg4844.Cell via ckzgPartialCells[i] = ckzg4844.Cell(partialCells[i]) - direct fixed-size array copy. Inside c-kzg-4844, cell_to_coset_evals operates on fixed-size array. Output cells part of ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs return value. makeCellsAndProofs processes these fixed-size arrays. No dynamic sizing anywhere.
attack_scenarios: Attacker cannot provide wrong-size Cell data: Go Cell type is fixed-size array, P2P deserialization into Cell enforces BytesPerCell bytes
Wrong content inside a Cell would produce invalid KZG proofs, caught by VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs in gossip validation
phase2.counterexample: No counterexample. Fixed-size array types in Go prevent cell size mismatches by construction.

phase2_5.adversarial_analysis: Go type system's fixed-size array semantics make cell size manipulation impossible from Go layer. An adversary providing cell bytes via P2P: the bytes must deserialize into fixed Cell type. Any extra or missing bytes in P2P message cause deserialization failure before Cell type is populated.
phase2_5.exploitation_feasibility: Not exploitable. Fixed-size array type guarantee in Go.

phase3.invariant_proving: Invariant: 'All Cell values have exactly BytesPerCell bytes'. Enforced by Go's type system - type Cell [BytesPerCell]byte is compile-time constant-size array. Cannot be violated at runtime by any Go code. Secondary invariant: 'Cell content represents valid field element evaluations' - enforced by KZG proof verification in gossip validation.
phase3.mathematical_guarantee: Go's type system provides compile-time guarantee that Cell values have exactly BytesPerCell bytes. This is a language-level invariant, stronger than any runtime check. KZG proof verification provides cryptographic guarantee of cell content correctness.

phase3_5.final_verdict: Not a vulnerability. Go Cell type (type Cell [BytesPerCell]byte) is a fixed-size array whose size is enforced at compile time. Cell size mismatches are impossible at Go type level. KZG proof verification in gossip validation cryptographically validates cell content. cell_to_coset_evals output size concern is handled by Go's type system and c-kzg-4844's fixed-size types.
phase3_5.reasoning: Cell type provides compile-time size invariant enforcement - stronger than any runtime check. VerifyDataColumnSidecar checks structural consistency, and VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs validates cell content via batch KZG proof verification. All three layers together ensure cell_to_coset_evals receives properly-sized and cryptographically-valid cell data.
